title: The Unpaid Work That Grows With the Climate

body.en: Efua has always fetched water, cooked, and cared for her mother-in-law alongside raising her own three children. None of that was ever easy, but it was manageable. Then the borehole near her house started running dry more often. Now the walk to the next-nearest water source takes an extra forty minutes, twice a day. Her mother-in-law's health has also worsened since the last heatwave, so there's more caregiving too. Nobody pays Efua for any of this work. It simply has to happen, and as the climate shifts, there is more and more of it landing on her specifically, while the hours in her day stay exactly the same.

followUpQuestion: What is one climate-driven change that added directly to Efua's unpaid workload?
